text:
Asha: Heads-up — putting together a proposal for fallback inspection & sampling UX for automatic rollouts. Need quick eyes.
Tom: TL;DR: we need a way to sample requests that hit fallback so product owners can audit quality without exploding logs.
Riley: Agree. Can we do adaptive sampling based on quota and severity? e.g. 1% baseline, ramp to 10% for high-error windows.
Marta: 👍 Also want to capture full request+model metadata (model, quant, route, region) but obfuscate PII.
Asha: Proposal sketch:
- sampling rules: rate, reservoir per-customer, error-triggered bursts
- UI: live sample counter, sampled-request explorer, export
- API: route-level flags => "fallback_sampling" config
Tom: Question: Should sampling live in the routing layer (fast, before enrichment) or post-handoff in telemetry? Latency tradeoffs.
Riley: Routing layer is best for accuracy (capture exact pre-fallback decision). We can add lightweight headers then enrich in async pipeline.
Marta: Concern: routing-level sampling can add perf jitter. Keep it tiny — increment a counter + enqueue id to sample queue. Nothing blocking path.
Asha: Example config (pseudo):
```
fallback_sampling:
  default_rate: 0.01
  burst_multiplier: 10  # for error spikes
  reservoir_per_customer: 50/day
  triggers: ["model_timeout", "500", "kv_cache_miss"]
```
Tom: On triggers — prefer semantic names over codes. e.g. "model_timeout" + "model_error_5xx" so UX doesn't force lookup of codes.
Riley: Need tie to quotas. If customer has strict privacy, reservoir_per_customer=0 unless allowed.
Marta: Add an allowlist for customers who want 100% capture for debugging.
Asha: Auditability: every sampled item gets an immutable audit-id; UI can replay request flow and show decision trace (why fallback chosen).
Tom: For replay we must strip any sensitive outputs. Maybe replay only metadata + anonymized prompts; provide secure download for enterprise.
Riley: Telemetry: add metrics: sampled_rate_by_trigger, sample_queue_backlog, replay_success_rate
Marta: UX: in console -> route config card show sampling status + last sampled timestamp + quick link to sample viewer.
Asha: API debate: Should route-level flag be part of rollout policy or separate telemetry policy? I lean rollout policy (keeps config near fallback rules).
Tom: If it's in rollout policy, rollbacks will also revert sampling which is good. But might clutter rollout UI.
Riley: Implementation note: when fallback occurs, router emits event: `fallback_hit` with fields {route, reason, model_id, customer_id, trace_id}. Sampler decides to persist.
Marta: Security note: sampled payloads must be encrypted at rest and access-gated by roles in console.
Asha: Ops question: what's the default sampling budget? We proposed 1% + bursts; does that feel safe for scale? Example calc: 10M requests/day * fallback_rate 0.5% => 50k fallback hits -> 1% sampling => 500 samples/day - OK.
Tom: Edge case: synthetic traffic from tests. Need to filter `internal_test=true` attribute before counting budget.
Riley: For low-volume customers we should use reservoir_per_customer to ensure we still capture at least N/day.
Marta: Implementation timeline: router changes (2w), event plumbing + async sampler (1w), console viewer + perms (2w) -> 5w total.
Asha: Action items:
- @Riley: draft router event schema and sampling hook (due Wed)
- @Tom: wire up telemetry metrics list + prometheus names (due Thu)
- @Marta: sketch console sample viewer UI and RBAC (due Fri)
- @Asha: write short spec for rollout policy integration (due next Mon)
Riley: I can take the schema. Quick Q — include raw latency histogram for request in sample? useful.
Marta: yes please.
Tom: 👍 I'm good with the plan. One more: add opt-out for customers via API flag.
deploy-bot: Deployment queue updated: branch `fallback-sampling/proposal` pushed to staging.
Asha: Great — I'll send the spec to the rollout-ux PR and tag you all. Thanks :raised_hands:
Marta: Nice. small follow-up: can sample viewer show anonymized tokens count instead of content? helps compliance.
Riley: We'll include that as option.
Asha: End.
